macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures edge higher as oil retreats and investors weigh U.S.-Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures rebounded after earlier volatility as oil prices steadied, with investors balancing renewed Middle East conflict risks against signs of temporary easing in energy markets. Reuters said the move reflected the market’s focus on whether the fighting could further disrupt inflation and broader risk sentiment.

items.title: Oil prices jump on fresh U.S. strikes against Iran
items.summary: Oil rose sharply after the U.S. launched fresh strikes against Iran, reviving concerns about the Strait of Hormuz and global supply disruption. Reuters reported that the rally also renewed inflation fears and pressured bonds and risk assets.

items.title: Asian and European equities stabilize after geopolitical shock
items.summary: Asian shares rose and European markets also recovered in choppy trading as semiconductor stocks bounced from recent selling. Reuters attributed the rebound to a pause in heavy risk-off positioning even as investors remained cautious about the Middle East conflict.

items.title: Japanese 10-year government bond yield hits 30-year high
items.summary: Japan’s benchmark 10-year government bond yield climbed to a 30-year high as higher oil prices renewed inflation concerns and investors remained wary about fiscal health. This added to global fixed-income pressure amid the broader geopolitical shock.

items.title: U.S. Treasury yields steady after recent spike
items.summary: U.S. 10-year Treasury yields held near recent highs after rising in the prior two sessions, with traders waiting for domestic economic data. Treasury markets were also absorbing the inflation implications of the Middle East flare-up.

items.title: ECB policymakers keep future rate path deliberately vague
items.summary: According to Reuters-summarized market coverage, European Central Bank policymakers agreed not to provide guidance on the future path of rates after June’s first hike since 2023. The minutes cited elevated uncertainty, reinforcing expectations that central banks remain data-dependent.

items.title: India inflation risks rise as fuel and food costs build
items.summary: Reuters reported that India’s consumer inflation likely moved back above the central bank’s medium-term target in June, driven by higher food and fuel prices, the U.S.-Iran war, and a weak monsoon. The development increases pressure on the RBI’s policy outlook.

items.title: China producer inflation accelerates to near four-year high
items.summary: China’s producer price inflation rose for a fourth straight month, reaching its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased. Reuters said the data indicated persistent cost pressure for domestic manufacturers.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast on Iran war fallout
items.summary: The IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast to 3% while warning that the Iran war is worsening global economic conditions. Al Jazeera reported that AI-related demand partly offset the energy shock in the revised outlook.

items.title: U.S. trade deficit surges amid AI spending boom
items.summary: The U.S. trade deficit widened to $77.6 billion in May as imports outpaced exports, with pharmaceuticals and semiconductors among the drivers. Al Jazeera said the jump reflected heavy artificial intelligence-related spending.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and crypto stocks slide as broad market selloff deepens
items.summary: Bitcoin fell sharply while crypto-linked equities tied to digital asset treasuries also tumbled, with Strategy, BitMine, Sharplink, Solana Company, and Upexi all seeing notable declines. CoinDesk said Bitcoin dropped to about $84,000 and its 20-index also moved lower.

items.title: European authorities seize $1.51 billion Bitcoin-mixing service
items.summary: Europol said it dismantled Cryptomixer, a crypto-mixing platform allegedly used by ransomware groups and darknet markets, and seized servers, data, and about $29 million in BTC. The move is one of the most significant enforcement actions in recent crypto crime news.

items.title: Canada moves toward stablecoin rules
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that Canada is considering a stablecoin regulatory framework, with Scotiabank describing the effort as aimed more at modernizing payments than reshaping broader financial markets. This is one of the clearest policy developments in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Ripple wins full MiCA CASP license in Europe
items.summary: NewsNow highlighted that Ripple secured a full MiCA CASP license, which would allow it to operate regulated payments across 30 EU countries. If confirmed by the underlying report, this would be a major regulatory milestone for the company in Europe.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins extend weekend weakness
items.summary: CryptoSlate’s market snapshot showed Bitcoin around $63,249.72, Ethereum near $1,746.80, XRP around $1.10, and Solana near $78.07, with several majors posting modest gains on the day but mixed 7-day performance. The broader tone remains cautious despite some intraday stabilization.

items.title: Polkadot drops below key support level
items.summary: CoinDesk reported that DOT plunged 11% and broke below the $2.05 support level, accelerating toward the psychological $2.00 area on heavy volume. This was one of the most notable token-specific price moves in the period.

items.title: Gleec acquires Komodo’s cross-chain DeFi stack
items.summary: CoinDesk said Gleec bought Komodo’s atomic-swap technology, token ecosystem, and core developers in a $23.5 million deal. The acquisition is a notable project-development story in blockchain infrastructure.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin outlines a long-term Ethereum rebuild
items.summary: CoinMarketCap reported that Vitalik Buterin described a 3-4 year 'Lean Ethereum' overhaul focused on quantum safety, privacy, cheaper data storage, and possibly replacing the EVM. This is one of the biggest project roadmap items surfaced in the last day.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent inside ChatGPT designed to perform tasks across multiple applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI software. The launch signals a push toward agentic workplace tools rather than standalone chat interfaces.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models for real-time conversation
items.summary: OpenAI also introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release expands OpenAI’s multimodal and voice-first product line.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning the company more directly against Anthropic and OpenAI in paid AI model access. The move broadens Meta’s commercial AI offerings beyond consumer products.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most capable model yet for coding and agentic work. The release continues the rapid cadence of frontier model updates among major AI labs.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said it appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The appointment highlights governance and safety oversight as a differentiator in advanced AI.

items.title: Anthropic’s advanced Claude models cleared for broader use
items.summary: The Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic’s latest Claude chatbot versions after a weekslong ban tied to cybersecurity concerns. The decision removes a major barrier to deployment of the company’s newest models.

items.title: New York Times-led publishers seek sanctions against OpenAI
items.summary: A group of newspapers led by The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging it misled the court about its ability to search its systems for evidence in the copyright case. The motion escalates the legal fight over training data and copyright.

items.title: Meta plans a massive data center in Alberta
items.summary: Meta announced it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand computing capacity for AI. The move reflects the continuing industry trend of aggressive infrastructure investment.

items.title: Google will disclose which ads are made with AI
items.summary: Google said it will now label ads that were created with AI. The policy change reflects growing pressure for transparency around synthetic media in advertising.

items.title: Meta’s AI chips expected to enter production in September
items.summary: Meta’s new AI chips are set to begin production in September, according to reporting from TechCrunch. The development underscores the industry-wide shift toward custom silicon to reduce reliance on outside chip suppliers.
